commits.edited_message:
rar5: Detect 32 bit size_t overflows

If a parsed value does not fit into 32 bit size_t, treat it as error
instead of truncating.

The name limits are byte counts: the header fields carry the length of
the stored name in bytes, and the decode buffers are sized in bytes via
MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES. Rejecting anything above MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 was a
leftover from when the limit was expressed in characters, and needlessly
fails archives with long multibyte names; only reject lengths that
cannot fit into the buffer at all.

Reported-by: krishna28238-arch <krishna28238-arch@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

Names are rejected above MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 bytes, so the decode
buffers never hold more than MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS bytes including the
terminator; drop the fourfold slack and size them to the limit.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is split between two commits that each touch a different half of the name-length invariant in the RAR5 reader, and neither half is unsafe without the other.

Commit 5335f6f ('rar5: Detect 32 bit size_t overflows') relaxes the acceptance bound: the filename check in process_head_file() and the link-target check in parse_file_extra_redir() change from MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 (2047) to MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1 (8191), on the rationale that the header fields carry byte counts and the decode buffers are MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (8192) bytes. Read on its own this is provably safe: __archive_read_ahead() guarantees the declared bytes exist, so at most 8199 bytes are written into an 8192-byte buffer. A 4096-byte name is simply accepted (verified: the tree of this commit alone accepts the PoC with ARCHIVE_OK, no sanitizer report).

Commit e8e74bd ('rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values') later 'right-sizes' the decode buffers: name_utf8_buf and target_utf8_buf shrink from MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (8192) to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS (2048), justified by the claim - true when the limit was written, false after 5335f6f - that 'names are rejected above MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1 bytes'. Read on its own this is also safe: with the 2047-byte check still rejecting long names, at most 2048 bytes are ever written (verified: reverting only the 5335f6f edit makes the PoC fail cleanly with 'Filename is too long').

Only the composition is unsafe: the relaxed check admits name_size up to 8191 while the shrunken stack buffer holds 2048 bytes, so memcpy(name_utf8_buf, p, name_size) in process_head_file() (and identically for link targets in parse_file_extra_redir()) writes up to ~6KB past the buffer. The PoC drives the public API (archive_read_open_memory + archive_read_next_header) with a well-formed RAR5 archive whose HEAD_FILE declares a 4096-byte name; AddressSanitizer aborts with a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE (rc 134). The original batch and the base both reject the same input cleanly, so the regime is new_defect.

Why the fix is non-local: neither diff contains a wrong statement in isolation - the bug is that the two constants (acceptance bound in one commit, buffer capacity in the other) no longer agree. Repairing it requires comparing the limit introduced by 5335f6f against the buffer sizing in e8e74bd and re-deriving the invariant (check bound + terminator <= buffer size) across both commits; each commit's own diff and message assert a locally consistent contract.

pocs.entry_point: archive_read_new + archive_read_support_format_rar5 + archive_read_open_memory + archive_read_next_header (libarchive public API)
